rows.ruling: Deployment identity gets its writer and its producer now. A node's identity is the SHA-256 of the qip-edge-node binary its unit starts. The startup script writes it to a read-only file the unit names, and refuses to start if it cannot. The centre's acceptable set is the digest the attested image payload records. qip-api reads it from a declared file. An unset file leaves the item unproduced, as ADR 0155 section 14 says. A file that is named but unreadable stops qip-api. A cell whose clock runs ahead of every venue it measures reads its clock as unavailable. That check uses the existing max_clock_skew and adds no new limit value. Credential expiry stays unreachable on paper (ADR 0155 section 15). No credential is minted to measure it: a real venue credential is a live surface ADR 0003 refuses. The row stays PARTIAL on that clause and does not count 'unreachable' as a measurement.
rows.closure: After the ADR, lane L1 builds three slices. (1) startup.sh.tftpl writes the sha256 of /usr/local/bin/qip-edge-node to a 0444 file, puts QIP_BUILD_IDENTITY_FILE in node.env, and refuses to boot on failure. Acceptance test in infrastructure.rs: the template writes the digest and names the file. Mutation: drop the line. (2) qip-api reads a declared build-set file into PolicyPayload::acceptable_builds. Test: a declared set is signed into the payload, an unset file leaves it unproduced, and an unreadable file stops start-up. Mutation: ignore the file. (3) qip-edge records the signed lead. clock_row reads Unavailable when every measured venue's stamp trails the cell's receive instant by more than max_clock_skew. Test: a cell whose clock runs ahead of every venue takes no new exposure. Mutation: restore the clamp at zero. The lane must also show that replaying the committed spools is unchanged. The lane writes docs/blueprint/lanes/l1-risk-4101-build-set-protected.patch, in which image.yml publishes the payload's qip-edge-node digest for qip-api. The row stays PARTIAL until a deployed node halts on an absent build and on the credential clause.

rows.ruling: Copies of one origin count once on every path that weighs evidence, not only in the fabric. The ruling admits a posterior can rise (an independent item no longer diluted by another origin's copies). It then judges that rise safe only because Platform::sizing_confidence (:18050) reads no posterior. But the red-team approval gate does read it. redteam.rs:568 takes effective_confidence, and :605 rejects below minimum_surviving_confidence. platform.rs:16537 then forms a proposal only for an is_actionable status. The tournament's detector vote also reads it (model_tournament.rs:812). So the change can flip a Rejected hypothesis to Approved, which loosens a guard on the decision path. Then never let a posterior move further from the prior than today's update would; take whichever of the folded and the current log-odds is nearer the prior. Any panic fails it, and the seed and the input are printed so the crash reproduces. A coverage-guided engine is reopened only by an ADR that names a crash class this gate missed.

Each runs a fixed regression seed set plus a bounded batch of fresh cases. The fresh seed derives from GITHUB_SHA when set and is fixed otherwise. rows.ruling: O21 is admitted narrowly. A release is refused before traffic moves when the plane's error budget is spent. After traffic moves, the same deploy.yml run that a person dispatched reads the plane's release decision. If the decision refuses, or cannot be read, the run moves traffic back to the previous promoted revision, rebuilds nothing, and fails. The incident is a drafted record for a person and is never sent outside (ADR 0213, R12-OBS-9158). No standing controller, no agent and no new credential rolls anything back.

It takes the decision URL, the service and the previous revision. On a refused or unreadable decision it runs 'gcloud run services update-traffic <svc> --to-revisions=<previous>=100', writes an incident draft to the job summary and exits 1. On an allowed decision it moves nothing. (3) qip-acceptance pipeline_scripts.rs test, with a fake gcloud on PATH: a_refused_or_unreadable_release_decision_moves_traffic_back_to_the_previous_revision_and_fails_the_run_and_an_allowed_one_moves_nothing. rows.ruling: A basket or an index carries its constituents and their weights. It is valued only from those constituents' prices. A position in it counts against its constituents' limits as well as its own, never instead of them. One with a missing weight, weights that do not sum to one, or an unpriced constituent is refused, not valued at a guess. A corporate action books in the ledger of record exactly once: a cash dividend as cash received against dividend income, a split or stock dividend as a unit change on the lot at unchanged cost. Under ADR 0153 decision 1 the operation itself is journaled, so the event log and the ledger hold one claim. It is all paper; no real dividend is paid or received.
rows.closure: Lane L6 (kernel/COVERAGE) claims the ADR number first. Add constituent weights to IndexDetails and StructuredProductDetails, refused when absent, non-positive, duplicated or not summing to one. Value from constituents, and count each constituent against its limits in addition to the direct position. Add a corporate-action OperationKind. Platform::apply_corporate_action pushes it onto desk_operations, and LotAdjusted carries it, deduplicated by the action key so a replay books nothing twice. Update the fixture of tests/asset_classes.rs::a_repo_an_index_and_a_basket_assemble_trade_on_paper_and_are_refused_without_their_class to state weights; no assertion is removed. Tests: (1) an index is valued from its weighted constituents and refused when a constituent is unpriced; mutation: drop one weight from the valuation. (2) A cash dividend and a split each book exactly one ledger operation, and a restart that replays LotAdjusted books neither again; mutation: skip the push in apply_corporate_action.

rows.ruling: I do not grant foundry lineages one by one. A lineage is evo-{subject}, minted per sweep at run time, and a register entry per lineage would be written to pass whatever the roots happen to run. A promotion is judged on the alpha family the sweep declared, one of the ten that ADR 0155 §24 already grants on paper, and a sweep that declares none is refused. Every root that builds a CentralConfig arms the register from the committed paper seed baked into its image, and fails closed when it cannot read it.
rows.closure: After the ADR: (1) StrategyFactory::promote judges the strategy subject by candidate.alpha_family(), refusing None with a message naming the sweep's lineage. The lineage stays the trial-book key. (2) infrastructure/docker/Dockerfile COPYs data/datasets/paper-eligibility.json to /etc/qip/eligibility/paper-eligibility.json. qip-api and qip-deepbrain read that fixed path in any deployed environment, and the repo copy only under QIP_DEPLOYMENT=local. Either refuses start-up with exit 78 when the file is unreadable or empty. No variable can disarm the register or point it elsewhere. (3) Venues and products come from the root's own committed configuration, and any the seed lacks is refused. The ADR may add records only for simulated subjects a root actually names (for example XSIM), paper jurisdiction only, under §24's existing grant, listed one by one. (4) Tests: a kernel test 'a candidate whose sweep declared no alpha family is refused promotion naming its lineage, while one declared momentum_and_trend on a recorded venue promotes' (mutation: fall back to the lineage key). A qip-deepbrain test 'the composed central plane is armed from the committed seed' (mutation: leave promotion_eligibility None). Every assertion in qip-kernel tests/central.rs::a_family_cleared_in_the_product_catalogue_but_unrecorded_in_the_compliance_register_cannot_be_promoted is kept. The row is re-graded on the lane's mutation report.

rows.ruling: D12 and ADR 0110 Amendment 1 stand. Every signing key is HSM in every environment. CMEK keys are HSM in stage and prod and may stay SOFTWARE in dev and test. The attestor moves to HSM as a new key beside the old one, never by replacing it: the old key carries prevent_destroy, and replacing it would wedge dev's apply. The old key keeps verifying until every running image is re-attested. Then it is disabled, never destroyed.
rows.closure: The lane writes the patch with these changes. variables.tf replaces kms_protection_level with signing_key_protection_level (default and only value HSM) and cmek_protection_level (SOFTWARE or HSM, default HSM, SOFTWARE only when var.environment is dev or test). main.tf passes the signing level to module.binaryauthorization and the CMEK level to secrets, registry, backup and evidence. build-pool.tf:52 and audit-logs.tf:72 take the CMEK level. outputs.tf:379 becomes one output per level. Dev and test tfvars set cmek_protection_level = "SOFTWARE", so no CMEK key is replaced. modules/binaryauthorization adds an HSM attestor key and lists both public keys on the attestor during the overlap. tests/kms-protection.tftest.hcl gains runs that refuse SOFTWARE signing in every environment and SOFTWARE CMEK in stage and prod, and that admit SOFTWARE CMEK in dev and test. Mutation: drop the environment validation and show the stage run fail. The parent applies the patch. The owner applies dev with its billing on, adding one HSM EC key version at about $2.50 a month (the per-key price in billed-plan §3), and re-attests running images before the old key is disabled.

It reaches seven sites: main.tf:249 (secrets), :605 (registry), :632 (evidence), :875 (binary_authorization) and :934 (backup), plus build-pool.tf:52 and audit-logs.tf:72. Only binaryauthorization's attestor is ASYMMETRIC_SIGN; evidence, backups, build-pool staging and asset_feed are encryption keys, so the split is right. The attestor has prevent_destroy (:77). billed-plan finding 2 and §4 say a level change replaces the key and wedges dev. D12 (owner-decisions-2026-10-11:49) and ADR 0110 Amendment 1 item 1 match the ruling. The §3 price of $2.50 per HSM key version is named, and no existing patch covers this, so WRITE_PATCH is right. Caveat the lane must handle: the closure says main.tf passes the signing level to module.binaryauthorization. Wired naively into the existing attestor key, that replaces it and causes the wedge the ruling forbids. If instead the old key is pinned to SOFTWARE everywhere, test, stage and prod would create a new SOFTWARE signing key on first apply, against D12. So the old SOFTWARE key must be pinned and must exist only in dev, where it is applied, behind a dev-only input. The HSM key must be the only attestor key elsewhere. kms-protection.tftest.hcl must also assert that no SOFTWARE ASYMMETRIC_SIGN key is planned outside dev, not just check the variable. The current default algorithm is RSA_SIGN_PKCS1_4096_SHA512, so the new EC key is a deliberate algorithm change.

Caveat: on a TLS data route, a caller with a mapped SAN and no bearer token is refused today and would be admitted after the change. That is ADR 0112's owner-accepted replacement, not a pure tightening. The lane should cite ADR 0112 for it and keep both new refusals: an unmapped SAN, and a bearer token that names a different identity. The 401 test at broker.rs:868 runs on plaintext and is not weakened.

rows.ruling: ADR 0113 §4 stands: the scouts' own project comes with the second region, not before, and node pools stay refused under ADR 0114 D4. What I take now is the network. The ingestion-discovery zone gets its own VPC, with no peering, VPN or route to any other network, and it reaches Google APIs only by private access. Its one sanctioned path to cognition goes through a Google-managed API under the zone's own identity, never through a route. Information-source egress leaves through its own router and NAT, which is planned only when a source entry is declared. The row stays PARTIAL on the project half.
rows.closure: After the ADR is claimed: declare a scout network and map ingestion-discovery to it. Make the egress router per network. Replace the cognition publish firewall path with a Google API grant to the zone's identity. Add egress.rs::the_scout_network_has_no_peering_vpn_or_route_to_any_other_network_and_alone_holds_information_source_egress. Mutation: add a google_compute_network_peering from the scout network to the service network and show the test fail. The change that first declares a source entry names the NAT's $5-$6 a month.
rows.adr_title: The scout zone gets its own VPC network with no peering or route to any other network, and its own project waits for the second region
rows.skeptic: Checked. trust-zones/main.tf local.zone_network (:39-53) puts ingestion-discovery on var.service_network_id, alongside ledger and treasury-write. sanctioned_egress_purposes (:141) gives it 'information-source'. core_paths has 'ingestion-discovery->cognition' = ['publish'] (:104). google_compute_router.egress (:503) has the one-network precondition (:518). Dev declares only application-identity, cognition, intelligence and management, with external_egress = {} at :129. ADR 0113 §4 puts the project split at the second region, and ADR 0114 D4 refuses node pools. This agrees with R12-GCP-8116. A VPC alone is free, and the $5-$6 NAT cost is named for when a source is declared. Notes for the ADR and lane: ADR 0113 §4 lists security, data, execution, services and engineering projects but no scouts project, so the ADR should name one. The scout VPC must be associated with the baseline firewall policy (infrastructure.rs:13931). gcp_placement.rs:550 already fails on any peering, so the new test needs to add the VPN and route checks to be worth having.

rows.ruling: O18 is decided once, under R12-SEC-10201's record: no agent identity pool and no per-run cloud credential. An agent run holds the sandbox's contents:read token and nothing else. Every workflow that can mint a Google credential refuses an agent before it authenticates. model-pack-publish.yml mints one and is missing from that list, and I close that gap by patch.
rows.closure: The patch makes three changes. It adds model-pack-publish.yml to dispatch_refused_for_agents.workflows in scripts/agent-policy.json. It adds the agent-guard.mjs dispatch step (--actor "$who" --workflow model-pack-publish.yml) before google-github-actions/auth in .github/workflows/model-pack-publish.yml. It adds a test to scripts/agent-guard.test.mjs that every .github/workflows file granting id-token: write is listed in dispatch_refused_for_agents. Mutation: remove model-pack-publish.yml from the list and show the new test fail. The parent applies the patch under decision 3, since it adds a refusal. The row stays PARTIAL until R12-SEC-10201's ADR and federation change land, and until agents push under a GitHub identity of their own.
rows.skeptic: Checked. Only these workflows grant id-token: write: deploy, drift, fleet, image, infra, model-pack-publish (:94) and vendor. Every one except model-pack-publish.yml is in dispatch_refused_for_agents, so the proposed 'every id-token workflow is listed' test passes once the patch lands and breaks no other workflow. ci.yml has no id-token. model-pack-publish.yml authenticates at :254 and has no agent-guard step. agent-guard.test.mjs:466 iterates only the listed workflows. judgeSandboxWorkflow (:556) refuses id-token (:566). The guard step form, --actor "$who" --workflow <file>, matches drift.yml. No existing lanes patch adds this, so WRITE_PATCH is right. It adds a refusal (decision 3 class) and agrees with R12-SEC-10201 and R12-SEC-10157. The lane should order it against R12-MODEL-10084's l2-model-pack-upload.patch, which edits the same workflow.

rows.ruling: Agents reach models only through the gateway, and only models on a committed approved list. A custom base URL is refused. So that a direct call fails, the gateway runs as its own identity and holds the only model grant, and the worker holds none. No provider key is approved for agents unless it is a Secret Manager secret mounted into the gateway alone. The Vertex preset uses the metadata token and stores no key, and it is the one approved route today. The gateway's identity writes each request's ledger line to a place the worker cannot write.
rows.closure: Now, as a tightening: model-gateway.mjs refuses any provider and model pair that is not in a committed approved list. Test in model-gateway.test.mjs: a custom base URL is refused before anything is sent. Mutation: admit 'custom' again and show the test fail. After the ADR: the gateway runs as its own service account in infrastructure/fleet holding aiplatform.user, and the worker's binding is removed. fleet.tftest.hcl asserts that the worker holds no aiplatform role and that only the gateway identity writes ledger/. The ADR names the gateway service's monthly cost before the fleet apply, which the owner runs.
rows.adr_title: Agents reach a model only through a gateway that holds the only model grant under its own identity, admits only a committed model list, and writes a ledger the worker cannot touch
rows.skeptic: Checked. model-gateway.mjs accepts ALGORIK_WORKER_BASE_URL (:204-216) and returns provider 'custom' (:312). The ledger is appendFileSync (:571) to LEDGER (:82). In fleet/main.tf, worker_project_roles adds roles/aiplatform.user when worker_may_call_models is true, which is the default (fleet/variables.tf:126). The fleet worker uses the vertex preset (worker.mjs:775), so refusing 'custom' now breaks nothing and only tightens. No test asserts that custom is admitted. Neither model-gateway.mjs nor infrastructure/fleet is a protected path. Moving the model grant to its own identity is a custody change under ADR 0102, so the ADR comes first. The ruling spends nothing now and requires the gateway's cost to be named before the owner's fleet apply. This agrees with R12-CICD-10116, where no model provider enters the sandbox.

rows.ruling: I do not buy the Security Command Center tier. Premium or Enterprise is a billed activation made at the organisation, and it stays declined under decision 5 of 2026-10-25, as R12-GCP-9086 already ruled. Nothing in the repository names its cost. The repository can assert what it already declares at no cost, so the two detectors and the mute configs get a plan test now. The row stays PARTIAL, because aggregation, threats and response integration exist only once the organisation activates a paid tier.
rows.closure: Add infrastructure/terraform/modules/scc/tests/detectors.tftest.hcl with a mocked google provider. Run 'the two detectors plan only when switched on and watch Binary Authorization and the private endpoint'. With enable_security_command_center = true, it asserts that both custom modules plan with enablement_state ENABLED and resource type container.googleapis.com/Cluster, and that their predicates read binaryAuthorization.evaluationMode and privateClusterConfig.enablePrivateEndpoint. With false, it asserts that no detector and no mute config plans. Mutations: drop either count guard, or change a predicate field; the run must fail on each. Rewrite the gap to name what remains: organisation activation at a paid tier with its monthly cost named first (the organisation administrator's act, declined for now), then the protected dev tfvars flip and a check that findings appear for the project. The row stays PARTIAL.
rows.skeptic: Verified. modules/scc/main.tf:41 and :80 are count-gated on var.enable_security_command_center. The mute config at :114 is for_each over var.muted_findings when the switch is on. All four tfvars set the switch false (dev:378, test:118, stage:118, prod:121). modules/scc has no tests directory, and no tftest or qip-acceptance file names scc. A mocked-provider plan bills nothing and touches no protected path. The ruling keeps SCC Premium declined, which is consistent with R12-GCP-9086, and the row stays PARTIAL. The predicates at :64 and :99 match the closure. One caveat for the lane: muted_findings defaults to {}, so 'no mute config plans when false' is vacuous as written. Both runs should set one muted_findings entry, and a mutation should drop the for_each guard.
